rust-build.title: Build a Rust project
rust-build.help: Uses the official rust image. Cargo's registry and the target folder are cached (Kubernetes).

node-build.title: Build a Node or Angular project
node-build.summary: npm ci then npm run build.
node-build.help: Runs the “build” script of your package.json. Each job runs its own npm ci: nothing is passed from one job to the next.

go-build.title: Build a Go project
go-build.summary: go build on the whole module.
go-build.help: Uses the official golang image. Match the image's version to the one in your go.mod.

rust-test.title: Test a Rust project
rust-test.summary: Cargo test on the whole project.
rust-test.help: Runs the unit tests and those of the tests folder. Put it after the code checks so badly formatted code is not tested.

node-test.title: Test a Node or Angular project
node-test.help: Runs the “test” script of your package.json. It must run without a graphical interface: if it needs a browser, choose an image that contains one.

go-test.title: Test a Go project
go-test.summary: go test on the whole module.
go-test.help: Runs all the tests of the module. Add -race to look for data races (slower).

python-test.title: Test a Python project
python-test.help: Installs requirements.txt then runs pytest: add pytest to your dependencies if it is not there already.

rust-format.title: Check Rust formatting
rust-format.help: Fails if the code is not formatted the way rustfmt would format it, without changing anything. The rust image does not include rustfmt: the job adds it.

rust-clippy.title: Analyze Rust code (Clippy)
rust-clippy.summary: Clippy, with warnings treated as errors.
rust-clippy.help: Spots common mistakes and clumsy constructs. The rust image does not include Clippy: the job adds it.

node-lint.title: Analyze Node or Angular code
node-lint.summary: npm ci then npm run lint.
node-lint.help: Runs the “lint” script of your package.json (ESLint, for example).

http-deploy.title: Deploy with an HTTP call
http-deploy.help: Kept by the “deploy” tag for a dedicated runner: without a runner that has it, the job stays pending. Create the DEPLOY_URL and DEPLOY_TOKEN secrets. A pipeline starts on every push: this job therefore redeploys every time.

http-notify.title: Notify a service (webhook)
http-notify.summary: Sends a POST request to an address.
http-notify.help: Handy to alert a chat or a tracking tool. Create the NOTIFY_URL secret with the full address (it often contains a token).

custom.title: Empty job
custom.summary: A light image and a command to replace.
custom.help: Alpine is a small Linux image with the basic commands. Change the image and the commands in the job's drawer.

shared.pathMessage: Letters, digits and . _ / ~ - only, with no space and no leading hyphen.
shared.k8sMessage: Lowercase letters, digits, - and .; starts and ends with a letter or a digit.
shared.kubeHelp: The job installs kubectl, writes the content of the KUBE_CONFIG secret (a kubeconfig file) where the tool looks for it, then acts on the cluster. For this, create a service account with rights limited to what is strictly needed (one namespace, a few object types), not administrator access.

docker-build.title: Build and publish a Docker image
docker-build.summary: docker build, then docker push to your registry.
docker-build.help: The runner does not give access to its machine's Docker: the build happens on a remote Docker daemon that you run, named by the DOCKER_HOST secret (tcp://host:2376). If it is protected by TLS, add the DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY and DOCKER_CERT_PATH secrets. Signing in to the registry uses the REGISTRY_USER and REGISTRY_PASSWORD secrets.

registry.label: Registry
registry.hint: Where to publish the image: registry.example.com, ghcr.io, docker.io…
registry.patternMessage: A server name, with a port if needed.

image.label: Image name
image.hint: The image's path in the registry, without the version.

tag.label: Version (tag)
tag.hint: FerrisGit provides neither a commit number nor a branch name to name the version: use a fixed name, “latest”, or a number you change by hand.

context.label: Build folder
context.hint: The folder sent to the daemon: “.” is the root of the repository.

login.label: Sign in to the registry
login.hint: With the REGISTRY_USER and REGISTRY_PASSWORD secrets. Untick for a registry without authentication.

push.label: Publish the image after the build

host.label: Server
host.hint: The name or address of the machine, reachable from the runner.
host.patternMessage: A machine name or an IPv4 address.

user.label: User
user.hint: The account to connect with: preferably an account dedicated to deployment.

verify.label: Verify the server's identity
verify.hint: Recommended: the SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS secret holds the server's fingerprint, obtained once with ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 vm.example.com. Without it, anyone posing as the server would receive your files.

ssh-run.title: Deploy to a VM (SSH)
ssh-run.summary: Connects over SSH and runs your commands on the machine.
ssh-run.help: The job installs the SSH client, drops the key from the SSH_PRIVATE_KEY secret, then runs your commands on the machine: restart a service, pull a new image with docker compose… Create a dedicated key pair, put the public key on the machine and the private key in the secret. A pipeline starts on every push: this job therefore runs again every time.

directory.label: Folder on the server
directory.hint: The commands start from this folder. Leave empty for the login folder.

commands.label: Commands to run on the server
commands.hint: One per line, in order; the next one only starts if the previous one passed.

ssh-copy.title: Copy files to a VM (SSH)
ssh-copy.summary: Sends a folder of the repository to the machine with rsync.
ssh-copy.help: Handy for a static site or an already built program: the folder is sent with rsync, only changed files travel. The files must exist in the repository: a job receives nothing from a previous job, so build them in this same job if needed. Same secrets as the SSH deployment.

source.label: Folder to send
source.hint: A folder of the repository. With a trailing slash (dist/), its content is sent; without one (dist), the folder itself.

destination.label: Folder on the server
destination.hint: Created if it does not exist.

delete.label: Delete on the server what is no longer in the folder
delete.hint: The server's folder becomes an exact copy. Avoid it if it contains anything else.

after.label: Commands to run on the server afterwards
after.hint: Optional: reload a service, for example. One per line.

k8s-apply.title: Deploy manifests to Kubernetes
k8s-apply.summary: kubectl apply on a folder of YAML files from the repository.

manifests.label: Manifests
manifests.hint: A YAML file or a folder of the repository.

wait.label: Wait for a Deployment's rollout to finish
wait.hint: Optional: the name of a Deployment. The job only passes once its pods are ready, and fails otherwise.

k8s-apply.help: {{ kubeHelp }} The manifests are the repository's, with the images already chosen: kubectl apply creates what is missing and updates the rest.

k8s-image.title: Update a Kubernetes Deployment
k8s-image.summary: Changes a Deployment's image, or restarts it, and waits until it is ready.

container.label: Container
container.hint: “*” updates all the containers of the Deployment.

image.label: Image
image.hint: The full reference, with its version.

wait.label: Wait until the rollout is ready
wait.hint: The job fails if the new pods do not become ready within three minutes.

k8s-image.help: {{ kubeHelp }} To deploy the version an earlier stage has just published, choose “Change the image” with the same reference. With the “latest” version, an unchanged reference restarts nothing: choose “Restart” instead.

helm-upgrade.title: Deploy with Helm
helm-upgrade.summary: helm upgrade --install on a chart from the repository or from a chart repository.

chart.label: Chart
chart.hint: A folder of the repository (./chart) or a name/chart reference.

values.label: Values file
values.hint: Optional: a file of the repository that adapts the chart.

create.label: Create the namespace if it does not exist

wait.label: Wait until everything is ready
wait.hint: The job fails if the release does not become ready within five minutes.

helm-upgrade.help: {{ kubeHelp }} The chart can be a folder of the repository (./chart). For a chart published elsewhere, first add its “helm repo add” command in the job's drawer.

pipeline.title: How it works
pipeline.body: A pipeline is a sequence of stages. Each stage contains jobs, the small tasks FerrisGit runs on every push: build, test, publish. The jobs of a stage start at the same time; a stage only begins once the previous one has passed.

stage.title: A stage
stage.body: A step of the pipeline. The jobs it contains run in parallel, and the next stage waits until they have all passed. If a job fails, the later stages do not start. Drag the cards from one column to another to change the order.

newStage.title: Add a stage
newStage.body: Give it a short name (test, build, deploy). It goes after the others; a stage's ⋮ menu lets you move it. An empty stage can be deleted.

job.title: A job
job.body: A task, run in a container: an image, then commands. Click the card to set it up. A job that fails stops the pipeline.

tiles.title: Tiles
tiles.body: Ready-made jobs for common needs. Pick one: it lands in the stage with an image and sensible commands, which you can then change.

name.title: Job name
name.body: It appears in the list of pipelines and lets other jobs wait for it. It must be unique.

image.title: Image
image.body: The container the commands run in: it brings the tools (rust:1 for Cargo, node:22 for npm, alpine for simple commands). A Docker Hub image is written name:version.

script.title: Commands
script.body: What the job runs, in order, as if you typed them in a terminal at the root of the repository. If a command fails, the job stops and is marked as failed.

insert.title: Insert a variable
insert.body: Puts the name of a variable or a secret into the command, as $NAME: it is replaced by its value when the job runs.

variables.title: Job variables
variables.body: Values the commands read by their name ($NAME). They are written in the repository's file: everyone can read them. For a password or a token, use a secret.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.body: Confidential values (token, password) stored encrypted for the repository, outside the file. Every job receives them as variables, and their value is masked in the logs. Just name them in a command: $NAME.

needs.title: Waits for
needs.body: By default a job waits for the whole previous stage. Tick jobs so it starts as soon as only those have passed, or to order two jobs of the same stage.

tags.title: Runner tags
tags.body: A runner is the machine that runs the job. If you give a tag, only a runner that has it takes the job: handy to keep a deployment for a specific machine. Leave empty for any runner.

cache.title: Caches
cache.body: Folders kept from one pipeline to the next to save time (downloaded packages, for example). Give a key: the same name shares the same cache. Only the Kubernetes engine applies them; with Docker runners they have no effect.

yaml.title: The YAML
yaml.body: The file FerrisGit actually reads. The cards and the YAML describe the same thing: change one, the other follows. In the YAML view, your comments are kept.

propose.title: Propose the change
propose.body: Nothing is written on the main branch: the file goes on a new branch with a merge request, which someone reviews and then merges.
